parties: Seamec Limited (target); acquirer identity undisclosed in public filing
headline: Seamec Limited files SEBI Takeover Regulation 31(4) disclosure of substantial acquisition with NSE.
sum: Seamec Limited has filed a mandatory Regulation 31(4) disclosure with NSE confirming a substantial acquisition event (≥25% voting rights acquired), but acquirer identity, consideration, and deal terms remain non-public in the headline filing. The marine and offshore oilfield services company's disclosure triggers SEBI takeover code compliance.
implication: Acquirer identity and deal value are gated in the full filed disclosure; counsel should obtain the complete Form DIS-2 or DIS-3 (filed with NSE) to advise clients on deal terms, source-of-funds checks, and open offer implications under Regulation 38 of the Takeover Code.
detail: Under SEBI's Substantial Acquisition of Shares and Takeovers Regulations, 2011 Regulation 31(4), any person acquiring 25% or more voting rights in a listed company must disclose the acquisition to the stock exchange within two trading days, along with the acquirer's identity, number of shares acquired, price/consideration, and source of funds. Seamec Limited's filing confirms a substantial acquisition event but the public headline disclosure does not specify the acquirer, share count, or deal value. The full disclosure document (filed with NSE) would contain these details and would trigger a mandatory open offer obligation under Regulation 38 if the acquirer is a new entrant or if shareholding crosses 55%. The specific consideration and structure of the acquisition will be evident only from the complete filed disclosure or any subsequent board announcement.

framework.ref: SEBI Substantial Acquisition of Shares and Takeovers Regulations, 2011 Regulation 31(4)
framework.note: Central: mandatory disclosure of substantial acquisition (≥25% voting rights) to stock exchange within two trading days; requires acquirer identity, number of shares, price, and source of funds.
Central: if acquisition results in voting rights ≥25% (new acquisitions) or ≥55% (any acquisition), mandatory open offer obligation triggered; 90-day acceptance period.
Central: restricts share transfer if acquirer identity is not disclosed to the company and exchange; central governance for takeover regulation.
Amended (2014, 2018): defines 'person acting in concert' and acquisition of 'voting rights'; relevant to understanding trigger thresholds.
Amended (2014): open offer pricing mechanism; acquirer must offer at the highest price paid in the preceding 26 weeks or fair value per SEBI methodology.

framework.ref: Foreign Exchange Management Act (FEMA), 1999 Section 3 & Schedule I
framework.note: If acquirer is foreign entity: relevant to source-of-funds disclosure and cross-border investment compliance.
Acquirer disclosure and shareholder approval requirements if acquisition results in change of control or material alteration of management.
Relevant to dematerialized shareholding transfers and acquisition mechanics in case of shares held in demat form.

Two-day disclosure deadline to NSE compliance requirement met

triggers.law: SEBI Substantial Acquisition of Shares and Takeovers Regulations, 2011 Regulation 31(4)
triggers.note: Mandatory disclosure trigger: acquisition of ≥25% voting rights in listed company.
Open offer trigger: if acquisition results in acquirer holding ≥25% (new) or ≥55% (any acquisition), open offer mandatory within 4 weeks of disclosure.
Disclosure and continuous updates of material acquisition events to market; timing and content gating.
